translations.answer: Massively parallel locomotion training is effective when environment count is paired with a sufficient rollout horizon, appropriate batch size, automatic terrain curriculum, and correct timeout bootstrapping; the reported 4,096-environment optimum and twenty-minute result are system-specific.
translations.applicability.assumptions.0: GPU-resident simulation and PPO are used.
translations.applicability.assumptions.1: Environment count, rollout horizon, and batch size are tuned together.
translations.applicability.controllers.0: PPO with joint-position actions and a PD inner loop.
translations.applicability.robots.0: ANYmal in the paper; the recipe requires revalidation for humanoids.
translations.confidence_rationale: Controlled parallelism, horizon, and timeout studies plus hardware transfer and public legged_gym code make this a strong systems result; numeric optima remain hardware-specific.
translations.evidence.0.locator: Figures 3–4 and 7; timeout and horizon ablations.
translations.evidence.0.note: Supports automatic curriculum and the interaction among parallelism, batch, horizon, and training time.
translations.evidence.0.title: Learning to Walk in Minutes Using Massively Parallel Deep Reinforcement Learning

translations.title: Does increasing only the number of parallel environments always make legged RL faster and better?
